title: The Cave That Swallowed the Heroes
subtitle: Nikumbha's illusion empties the Yadava ranks, one hero at a time.
story:
As the clear sun rose over the plain, the mountain gave birth to an army. From the mouth of Shatpura cave the Danavas came roaring, a host spilling out on asses, elephants, crocodiles, hares, horses, buffaloes, lions and tortoises, with chariots drawn by the same wild beasts, and the sound of trumpets, wheels and conches rising like a storm that had learned to march.

The war that had begun at the crowded sacrifice had carried the Yadava host to this plain, and they had come prepared for everything but this. Krishna, Baladeva and Satyaki had ridden to the field on Garuda's back, bathed in the waters of the sacred river Avarta, and worshipped Shiva before the first arrow flew. Pradyumna stood at the head of the army, and the Pandavas kept guard over the sacrifice ground behind them. At Krishna's mandate the war-bugles sounded, and Samba and Gada drew the host up in the shape of a great crocodile, while Sharana, Uddhava, Viprithu, Prithu, Sudangshthra, Vichakshu and the rest held the rear with Aniruddha. And above, where only Krishna could see them, hovered Jayanta and Pravara, summoned by a single thought.

The kings of the earth had chosen sides. Among those who came to aid the Asuras stood the followers of the Chedi king Shishupala, the hundred brothers of the Kuru house headed by Duryodhana, and rulers such as Bhagadatta, Shalya, Shakuni and Jarasandha, drawn into the gathering storm. At the head of the whole host came Nikumbha, as the lord of gods issues out at the head of the celestial host, only darker; and behind him the Asura ranks filled earth and sky with their leonine cries.

The battle opened with arrows like serpents. Nikumbha's shafts fell on the Yadava army like a rain of poison, and Anadhrishti, commander-in-chief of the Yadu host, could not bear it. He answered shaft for shaft, his feathered arrows clearing the enemy ranks, until the air grew so thick with missiles that Nikumbha himself, with his chariot, his standard and his horses, disappeared from sight. It was an insult the great Asura would not bear: anger kindled in him, and with it the decision to fight with what no arrow could touch.

That was when the field learned its true enemy. Nikumbha, foremost of those who wield illusion, was not hiding. He was working. By his illusive powers he bewildered Anadhrishti where he stood, carried him to the cave of Shatpura, and imprisoned him there. Then he returned to the field and did it again. Kritavarma. Charudeshna. Vaitarana of Bhoja's race. Sanatkumar. Arksha, the son of Jambavati. Nishatha and Ulmukha. And after them, one by one, countless more Yadava heroes, each led dazed and helpless into the dreadful cave while the shape of Nikumbha himself was so completely hidden that no one could see him come or go.

It was a war fought by subtraction. The Yadava ranks did not fall. They vanished. A captain would be standing there shouting orders, the dust would shift, and he was gone, swallowed by the mountain. The army could answer spears and arrows; it could not answer a man who was never where it looked.

When the truth of it sank in, rage came to the Yadava side such as the plain had not seen. Krishna, Baladeva, Satyaki, Samba, the irrepressible Aniruddha, and Pradyumna above them all, who had watched their kinsmen led into the dark, were filled with anger. They had come to fight a war; they found themselves watching a prison being filled.

Krishna looked at the cave, and then at the host that had done this. He set string to his Sarnga bow, and the note it made silenced the battlefield.

The fire was about to range on grass.
reflection: The battle turns on an enemy who fights by theft rather than slaughter, taking warriors whole instead of killing them. Against a power that hides itself, no formation avails, and the story's edge is that the fury which finally answers it belongs not to the army but to Krishna alone.
content_note: Battle violence with restraint: warriors are captured and imprisoned rather than killed.
next_story_tease: But the Sarnga bow was already strung.
hero_scene: Nikumbha, half-shimmering with illusion, leading the bewildered Anadhrishti toward the black mouth of Shatpura cave while the battlefield blurs behind them with dust and arrows, and in the distance Krishna's eyes blaze with anger as he reaches for his bow.
